label: yes
controls_available: Start Engine begins the active driving phase.
After start, LEFT, CENTER, and RIGHT panel buttons set persistent steering to -1, 0, and 1.
After start, BRAKE, COAST, and THROTTLE panel buttons set persistent pedal to -1, 0, and 1.
FILE DELIVERY is administrative; keyboard input is not the selected control surface in simplified mode.
autonomous_processes: After start, requestAnimationFrame/pump advances 20-ms physics ticks from elapsed task time without a new control click.
The yellow car's speed, heading, and position integrate on every tick under the last persistent steering and pedal settings.
Traffic cars advance along their lanes and update speed and braking from projected conflicts and same-lane gaps; their lane positions wrap at cycle limits.
Collision, road-edge, arrival, and timeout status can arise during the active ticks, after which physics stops.
grouped_control_modes: D: post-start simplified panel-button driving settings, with persistent steering LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT crossed with pedal BRAKE/COAST/THROTTLE (nine combined settings).
A changed steering-button or pedal-button click is a panel_buttons control event; clicking the already selected setting is ineffective.
START ENGINE and FILE DELIVERY are administrative boundaries, not outcome-affecting control modes.

clause_i.reason: The difficulty-1 generator still samples each traffic phase, speed, yielding horizon, and deceleration from the seed. Histories with the same prior actions and task times can therefore have a clear exit or a slower car closing the yellow car's path, requiring different delayed steering/pedal choices. An action-history-only q cannot distinguish those histories.

clause_ii.reason: The configured bounded window is 400 ms with five chronological frames. The canvas visibly shows every traffic car, its lane position, the yellow car, and red brake lamps; consecutive positions reveal direction and relative closing speed. That recent visual evidence is sufficient to choose the delayed panel setting for the observed traffic situation.

clause_iii.reason: Using the same moving traffic stream, a slower car can advance into or along the right-turn departure path during a 400-ms delay. In a still-clear, safely spaced state, a right-turn/throttle setting is useful; after the visible gap closes, that setting has lower outcome value or lower advantage because it can produce rectangular-body contact, while coast or brake can still preserve a route. The loss is caused by traffic/physics state evolution, not by a deadline or a fixed wait.

common_visible_process: The seeded crossing traffic continuously changes position and braking state relative to the yellow car. Its recent visible trajectory and brake lamps determine whether an accelerating right-turn control remains safe and useful after the delay.

pre_run.reason: render initializes control to [0, 0] and started to false, while setControl returns before started is true. Thus preparatory simplified clicks cannot arm steering or throttle. Start begins the autonomous phase; with no post-start outcome-affecting action, pedal remains neutral, initial speed is zero, and the neutral drag update keeps the yellow car stationary, so it cannot reach the goal for any seed.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 is one lane, two cars, speeds 26-32, yielding horizons 2.0-2.4, right turn only, and road_half 100; simplified mode uses persistent panel settings; the frame window is 400 ms with five frames.
The environment exposes a frame window at 10 fps and repeats the 120-second, 400-ms, five-frame runner settings.
The seed changes turn and traffic phase, speed, yielding horizon, deceleration, and color; the generated world contains moving traffic, physics constants, and the right-turn goal.
The browser advances ego and traffic state on each tick, recomputes responsive braking/conflicts, persists panel controls, and uses elapsed time to pump ticks without new actions.
Start begins the run; the canvas renders the road, goal, cars, yellow vehicle, and braking lamps; the simplified HTML binds the six panel buttons to panel_buttons events.
The authoritative replay applies the same ego/traffic physics, rectangular collision and road checks, and goal test; simplified transcripts must use panel_buttons and arrive successfully.

The ordinary-UI solver evaluates physical continuations including braking drivers and repeatedly updates simplified panel controls while the world runs, corroborating that traffic observations affect control selection.
Task verification loads the exported result and independent Courtesy Junction replay grader.
The used verifier helper reads the exported task result as a JSON object and returns it to the verifier.
